$comment: Dialect: JSON Schema draft-07. The dialect keyword is intentionally omitted so nothing has to be fetched over the network to validate this file; scripts/audit/required_checks_truth.py selects jsonschema.Draft7Validator explicitly.
title: SYNAPSE required status-check declaration
description: Schema for infrastructure/quality/required-checks.yaml (E1.7; R14.1). scripts/audit/required_checks_truth.py validates the file against this schema before resolving each declared job against the workflow that defines it (R14.2). Structural validity is a precondition of the consistency check, not a substitute for it: a schema-valid file whose jobs do not resolve still FAILs.

branch.description: The protected branch whose required-check set this file declares.

required.description: The declared required set. Every entry must report on every pull request to `branch`.

candidates.description: Eligible but not declared required. Never treated as required.

ineligible.description: Jobs that cannot be a required status check as currently triggered. Not an exemption from gating -- a statement that branch protection cannot cover them.

pending.description: Jobs that join `required` once they exist. Job names here are deliberately NOT resolved.

jobRef.description: A workflow job id as written under `jobs:`.

check_name.description: What GitHub matches: the job's `name:` if present, else the job id. Must byte-match the workflow.

gates.description: The gates this job executes, so R14.3's document-to-job mapping is checkable.

detail.description: The trigger or condition that makes the job ineligible, in enough detail to re-derive from the workflow file.

check_name.description: null while the job does not exist. A pending entry never contributes a required check.

status.description: I-7: `unverified` is a first-class state and is never a pass. Only a run that read the live configuration may write `verified` or `mismatch`.

allOf.description: A `verified` or `mismatch` status requires a real read: read_at and contexts must both be populated (R14.5, R14.6).

read_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the read performed during the reporting run (R14.6). null means no read has happened.

contexts.description: The live required-status-check contexts as returned by the hosting platform.
